pages.lesson:
LESSON: CHANGE OF STATE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: MATTER
Topic 2.1: Change of State

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Change of State. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How is change of state of matter important in day-to-day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled
2. describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life
   In simple words: practise until you can describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Change of State using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Change of State in the examples.
2. Explain Change of State to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Change of State.
4. Show that you can: identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Change of State using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Change of State important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss the applications of change of state of matter in everyday life,
2. Make candles using waste candle wax or beeswax.
3. Communication and collaboration: The learner acquires speaking and listening skills as they brainstorm the meaning of change of state of matter.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled
2. describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
